title: Creating Repositories, Staging & .gitignore
description: Initialize new Git repositories, master file tracking lifecycles with git status and git add, and exclude unwanted files with .gitignore.

blocks.content: You have edited two files, but only one is ready to save as history. You need to choose the exact change you are recording. What is the smallest Git action that keeps the work safe?

Your working directory contains current files. The staging area is the deliberate preview for the next commit. Use `git add file-name` to stage only the change you intend to save.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["Working files"] -->|"choose an action"| B["Git history"] -->|"share or recover"| C["Team project"]
```

blocks.question: You changed two files but want to commit one. What do you use?
blocks.explanation: Staging lets you select the exact changes for the next commit.

blocks.prompt: Model the Git idea in a tiny simulator. Export a function named `stageFile` that takes `(working, staged, file)` and returns a new staged list containing `file` once. Do not change either input list.

tests.description: works when no working files are listed yet
keeps an already staged file while adding another
